How to read this

  • A scenario is one version of the future budget. BASE is the current-law baseline: what happens if nothing changes. It is always on the chart. DEC is the decided program laid on top of it.
  • Nominal dollars are the dollars of each year. Real dollars remove inflation, using the {{DEFLATOR}} and expressed in dollars of FY{{BASE_YEAR}} (assumption). % of GDP compares each figure with the size of the economy that year, which is the fairest way to compare far-apart years.
  • A deficit is one year's shortfall. Debt held by the public is the running total owed. Net interest is what the government pays to carry that debt.
  • Numbers are estimates from the project's fiscal model, built on CBO's February 2026 baseline. They are not forecasts.
  • Every figure on this page is copied from the model's generated files when the page is built. Nothing here is typed by hand.

The D4 tests

D4-B is the fiscal rule Espen decided in the second decision brief. Each row is one test; the result is the model's own.

{{D4_TABLE}}

General-fund reading beside the unified reading

The maturity test reads the general fund only. The debt guardrails read the unified budget, where Social Security's new payroll revenue lowers total debt (assumption). Under the decided rule the general-fund debt is shown for information, not as a guardrail. Both are in % of GDP. The general-fund reading is the debt the general fund adds. The unified reading adds the dedicated channels, mainly Social Security's surplus, and is what moves total debt held by the public; negative means below the baseline.

{{GFU_TABLE}}

Interest-rate stress case

The same program and the same baseline with interest rates one point higher on all debt, from the start year the assumption gives (assumption). The D4 tests themselves are judged at CBO's rates.

What this does not show yet

  • Budget authority versus outlays, and the appropriation types. They come with piece B3, the provision library. Today the viewer shows outlays and revenue only.
  • Cautious-end readings. The fiscal model carries midpoint estimates only; the low and high ends of the ledger do not reach it. So no test here has a "cautious" result beside it.
  • The decided program by category in dollars. The model keeps the program's categories only as shares of GDP in a few years; the category chart shows the baseline.
  • Other deflators and base years. Real dollars use the single default shown above.
